module_title: Important Lakes and Waterfalls - Basic Superlatives
introduction: Lakes and waterfalls are crucial freshwater resources and major tourist attractions. For basic competitive exams, mastering the 'superlatives' (largest, longest, highest) of India's lakes and waterfalls is the first mandatory step.

core_concepts.title: Wular Lake (Jammu & Kashmir)
core_concepts.description: It is the largest freshwater lake in India. It is fed by the Jhelum River and was formed as a result of tectonic activity.

core_concepts.title: Chilika Lake (Odisha)
core_concepts.description: It is the largest brackish water (salty) lagoon in India and the second largest in the world. It is located at the mouth of the Daya River.

core_concepts.title: Vembanad Lake (Kerala)
core_concepts.description: It is the longest lake in India. It is a famous 'Kayal' (backwater) where the annual Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race takes place.

core_concepts.title: Kunchikal Falls (Karnataka)
core_concepts.description: Located on the Varahi River in the Shimoga district of Karnataka, it is the highest waterfall in India (approx. 455 meters).

important_entities.name: Jog Falls
important_entities.significance: Located on the Sharavati River in Karnataka. While Kunchikal is the highest overall (it falls in tiers/steps), Jog Falls is famous as the highest direct untiered 'plunge' waterfall.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Chilika is the largest 'coastal/lagoon' saline lake. However, 'Sambhar Lake' in Rajasthan is India's largest 'inland' salt lake. Read the question carefully!

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Associate 'Vembanad' with 'Long' to remember it is the longest lake in India.

exam_strategy_tips: Always memorize the river associated with a waterfall. Jog = Sharavati. Kunchikal = Varahi. Dhuandhar = Narmada.
Superlatives are heavily tested: Largest Freshwater (Wular), Largest Saline (Chilika), Longest (Vembanad).
